title: Halden Sleep wholesale mattress catalog: match a twelve-SKU two-setup packshot batch to one house white point, triage boxed-vs-styled treatments, recolor a colorway, vectorize the wordmark, and data-merge one press-ready spec sheet per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief in which a boxed-mattress vendor had 'product descriptions and a clean image set already prepared' and needed the specification-bearing catalog material a marketplace/retail intake team approves (sizes, materials, firmness, certification, weight, packaging dimensions). Laundered to the fictional brand 'Halden Sleep' — no real company, marketplace, product, or trademark is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original implied a multi-product grid catalog, which is NOT connector-doable — document_merge_data_layout emits exactly ONE FILE PER ROW and cannot place several records on one page, and a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind merge fields — and it implied hand-cleaning the roster data, which no Adobe connector can do. So the job is modeled as what the tools genuinely produce and reward: the client hands over a genuinely hand-authored single-record InDesign spec-sheet template (.indd, ONE product per A4-landscape page) carrying live <<fields>> plus one @-prefixed image-path column, a clean authored roster CSV whose copy binds verbatim, twelve raw product packshots shot across TWO lighting setups (a cool softbox bay and a warm ambient room) each carrying a photographic 18% grey card in frame, and a flat wordmark scanned on off-white stock. The Adobe chain does the real work: neutralize every packshot to its own in-frame grey card so the whole set shares one white point; TRIAGE the two packshot kinds to different correct treatments (the compressed-box shots on studio seamless get knocked onto a pure-white PDP ground by removing the outer background; the rolled-out-mattress shots in a styled room set are graded and reframed in place and must NOT be knocked out); recolor one model's cover-gusset colorway without a reshoot; prep-and-vectorize the scanned wordmark; then merge the authored template against the roster to emit one press-ready 300 DPI spec sheet per SKU.
one_line_ask: Bring Halden Sleep's twelve mixed-lighting mattress packshots to one house white point by neutralizing each to the grey card it carries, decide per frame how far to move white balance without killing any cover's true color, triage the boxed-on-seamless shots (knock to pure white PDP by removing the outer background) apart from the styled room-set shots (grade and reframe in place, no knockout), deepen one model's sage cover-gusset to the forest colorway without reshooting, prep and vectorize the scanned wordmark, then data-merge the client's authored single-record InDesign template against the roster to produce one press-ready spec sheet per SKU.
full_brief: Halden Sleep is a boxed-mattress startup taking its 2026 line wholesale, and before the retail-partner intake team will approve us we need a proper spec sheet for every model — one clean A4-landscape sheet per SKU carrying the size, cover material, firmness, certification, weight and packed-box dimensions, with a high-quality product shot and our wordmark crisp at the top. We are NOT reshooting. Here is the problem with the twelve photos we are handing you: they were taken across two setups on two different afternoons. Roughly half were shot square-on in our little studio bay under a cool softbox — those are the compressed models still in their printed sleeve, sitting on a light-grey paper sweep. The other half are the rolled-out mattresses, styled on a bed platform in a warm-lit room set so buyers can see the quilted top and the side profile. Straight out of the folder the set is a jumble — some cool and slightly blue, some warm and orange, a couple shot a few degrees off level — and a catalog of mismatched shots reads cheap to an intake reviewer. To give you an honest target we laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every single frame. Your job on the photos: bring the whole set to one consistent, true-to-product look by neutralizing each shot to the grey card it contains, so once every card reads a clean neutral the entire catalog sits at one shared white point and brightness — a reviewer scrolling the sheets should not be able to tell which afternoon a shot came from. Straighten any shot that is sitting slightly off level. Keep every cover's real color true — some of these covers are genuinely dark or richly colored, and the set should show them as they actually are, not tinted by the afternoon they were shot in. For how each product is presented: the models we sell boxed should read as clean catalog product shots — the box on pure solid white like a PDP, with the studio sweep and the grey card gone. The styled room-set shots are our lifestyle look — keep the bed platform and the room; just grade them, level them, and reframe them cleanly with the grey card cropped out of shot. Two more things. We sell the Terra Hybrid in two cover colorways and only shot the sage one; give us a second, deeper forest-green version of that same shot for the alternate colorway, moving only the cover gusset/piping and keeping every quilt shadow and highlight real — no flat painted-on color, no whole-image tint bleeding onto the bedding. And our wordmark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper — get it clean and razor-sharp as vector art for the sheet masthead. Finally, build the sheets: we have hand-built the InDesign spec-sheet template with the real placeholder fields and image slots, and we are giving you the roster; merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page sheet with its specs bound and its matching finished photo dropped in, then hand back a press-ready 300 DPI PDF, one page per model, with the Terra Hybrid — our flagship — leading as the first page. Bind our copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our specs or prices. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point; the boxed shots on clean white; the room-set shots untouched-in-place and reframed; the colorway variant natural under the existing light; the wordmark a crisp vector; and exactly one finished sheet per roster row. Tell us, for each photo, the white-balance and exposure adjustments you applied, so we can see the set was matched deliberately.

inputs.name: halden_speccard.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 LANDSCAPE (297x210 mm) mattress spec sheet — ONE product per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<sku>>, <<model>>, <<size>>, <<firmness>>, <<material>>, <<height_in>>, <<weight_lb>>, <<cert>>, <<box_dims>>, <<price>>, a masthead image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path merge column (@wordmark) so the merge drops the vector wordmark into the masthead, and ONE product-image frame wired to a second @-prefixed image-path merge column (@image) so the merge drops the matching finished packshot into the sheet. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-up grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a 2-up spread would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @-image-path columns (product photo @image, masthead @wordmark), and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record spec sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (the original 2-up spread is impossible). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. The audit-era version made this a report; here it is the composed print endpoint.

inputs.name: halden_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a clean, consistent authored product-roster CSV, exactly 12 rows, columns exactly: sku,model,size,firmness,material,height_in,weight_lb,cert,box_dims,price,@image,@wordmark. ROW 1 is the flagship Halden Terra Hybrid (it leads the merged PDF as page 1), then Halden Cloud 10, Halden Drift Memory, Halden Summit Firm, Halden Graphite Cool, Halden Nimbus Plush, Halden Ridge Hybrid, Halden Meadow Latex, Halden Aspen Medium, Halden Cove Soft, Halden Vale Firm, Halden Basalt Hybrid — one row per model with realistic wholesale mattress specs. Firmness from the controlled set Soft/Medium/Medium-Firm/Firm; all linear dimensions in INCHES and weight in POUNDS (consistent units, no cm/kg drift); price formatted $#,###.## consistently; every sku unique. The @image column names the matching FINISHED packshot file the agent will produce (e.g. @terra_packshot.jpg, @cloud10_packshot.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each processed photo into that row's single-record sheet; the @wordmark column holds the SAME vector wordmark file on every row (@halden_wordmark.svg) so the merge also drops the crisp wordmark into each sheet's masthead frame. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the two @-prefixed image-path columns. The roster is CLEAN — the agent binds it verbatim and does not rewrite it.
inputs.realism_notes: Honors the brief's 'product descriptions and detailed specs already prepared'; headers match the authored .indd fields and the two @-image columns (@image product photo, @wordmark masthead) so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy AND the correct photo per SKU AND the shared vector wordmark. 12 rows => the merge produces exactly 12 finished sheets; row 1 (Terra Hybrid) becomes page 1 of the merged PDF (the flagship hero page — no separate per-record export exists). Copy binds verbatim (no connector can edit a CSV), keeping the task inside connector bounds.

inputs.name: cloud10_boxed_packshot.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal square-on e-commerce packshot of a COMPRESSED boxed mattress standing upright in a printed cardboard sleeve with a printed carry-handle graphic near the top, on a light-grey studio paper seamless. A photographic 18% neutral grey card and a small white chip lie flat on the sweep at the lower-left edge. Shot under a COOL softbox with a distinct blue-cyan cast, slightly flat and marginally under-exposed, straight off the camera, un-graded. Real cardboard print texture and sleeve edge, soft contact shadow. Full-frame camera capture, approx 3800 px long edge, not CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Halden Cloud 10, BOXED kind, Setup A (cool softbox). Grey card in frame is the neutralization target; the seamless + card are removed by the knockout-to-white treatment, which isolates the OUTER background only (no enclosed interior hole is punched). Camera-scale so the 300 DPI sheet frame is reached by downscale.

A photographic 18% neutral grey card and a small white chip rest on the nightstand at the frame edge. Full-frame camera capture, approx 4400 px long edge, un-graded, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Halden Terra Hybrid, ROLLED kind, Setup B (warm ambient), tilted ~3deg (needs straighten). This is the recolor hero: its sage cover gusset is deepened to the forest colorway in a separate masked pass. Styled room set => must be graded and reframed in place, NEVER knocked out (removing the platform/room would destroy the styling). Grey card is cropped out in the reframe.

inputs.name: graphite_rolled_packshot.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal styled shot of a ROLLED-OUT mattress with a GENUINELY DARK CHARCOAL / graphite quilted cover on a bed platform in a room set, shot under NEUTRAL balanced light (no warm or cool cast) so the scene is already close to correct white balance, level. A photographic 18% neutral grey card and white chip sit at the frame edge and ALREADY read close to neutral. Real charcoal-fabric weave and quilt shadowing, natural soft shadow. Full-frame camera capture, approx 4400 px long edge, un-graded.
inputs.realism_notes: SKU Halden Graphite Cool, ROLLED kind, THE TRAP. The cover is really dark charcoal and the light was neutral, so the in-frame grey card already reads neutral — the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (match exposure/brightness to the set only). An agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool' or 'cool the warm' correction, or that cools an imagined cast, neutralizes this card off-neutral and turns the charcoal cover a muddy blue-grey, stripping the real product color. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: halden_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Halden Sleep' wordmark inked on off-white textured paper: a calm modern sans-serif with a small crescent-moon mark, deep slate-blue letters. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/separate from the ground, crop to the mark, knock the off-white to transparency, THEN vectorize. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering.

outputs.name: Halden_SpecSheets_perSKU_x12.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly twelve press-ready A4 landscape (297x210 mm) spec sheets — ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 12) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet binds its sku/model/size/firmness/material/height_in/weight_lb/cert/box_dims/price verbatim from the roster with its matching finished packshot dropped into the @image frame and the vector wordmark dropped into the @wordmark masthead frame; ~300 DPI press quality. The flagship Halden Terra Hybrid is roster row 1, so it leads as page 1 of the merged PDF — the 'hero' is simply the first page, there is no separate per-record export. Acceptance gate: if fewer than 12 pages, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

outputs.name: neutralized_masters_cardbearing_x12
outputs.spec: Twelve retained neutralized full-resolution masters — the per-frame white-balance/exposure-corrected frames BEFORE any knockout or reframe, each still carrying its in-frame 18% grey card. This is the card-BEARING artifact the grader measures neutrality on, because the delivered packshots have the card removed (boxed knockout) or cropped out (room reframe). Accompanied by the per-frame report of the white-balance (temp/tint) and exposure adjustments the agent applied. Acceptance (grader-checked on THESE card-bearing masters, which retain the card): every grey card reads visually neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance) and all twelve sit at one shared white point and brightness; the Graphite Cool master shows essentially no white-balance shift with its charcoal cover held true; no white clipped to 255 / no black crushed to 0; the reported per-frame moves are non-identical across the two lighting setups.

outputs.name: graded_packshots_x12
outputs.spec: Twelve finished packshots derived from the neutralized card-bearing masters: the five compressed-box shots isolated onto a pure solid-white PDP ground (#FFFFFF) with the seamless and grey card gone (image_remove_background isolates the outer background only); the seven styled room-set shots leveled where tilted and reframed with the grey card cropped out and the room styling left in place (NOT knocked out); the Graphite Cool cover held at its true charcoal. Acceptance (grader-checked HERE): the grey card is ABSENT from every delivered file (removed by the knockout on the boxed shots, cropped out on the room-set shots); the boxed shots sit on #FFFFFF; the room-set shots are un-knocked with their styling intact; the finished set reads as one cohesive white point and brightness (traceable to the card-bearing masters); no white clipped to 255 / no black crushed to 0. Grey-card NEUTRALITY itself is graded on neutralized_masters_cardbearing_x12, never on these card-excluded files.

outputs.name: variant_terra_forest_colorway.jpg
outputs.spec: Alternate-colorway variant of the Terra Hybrid: the sage-green cover gusset/piping deepened to the forest-green house colorway via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass pair (a small within-family green hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance settle that deepens the sage — an in-band adjacent shift, NOT a near-complementary rotation) riding the gusset's existing luminosity, so the quilt shadows, stitching and highlights stay natural and the bedding, platform and room are untouched — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill.

outputs.name: halden_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: cloud10_boxed_packshot.jpg, terra_rolled_packshot.jpg, drift_boxed_packshot.jpg, summit_rolled_packshot.jpg, graphite_rolled_packshot.jpg, nimbus_boxed_packshot.jpg, ridge_rolled_packshot.jpg, meadow_boxed_packshot.jpg, aspen_rolled_packshot.jpg, cove_boxed_packshot.jpg, vale_rolled_packshot.jpg, basalt_rolled_packshot.jpg, halden_wordmark_scan.png, halden_speccard.indd, halden_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the twelve packshots, the wordmark scan, the authored .indd template and the roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload — plumbing, not counted as difficulty.

Cloud 10 (BOXED, Setup A cool): WARM the temperature and set tint until the in-frame grey card reads neutral, lift exposure to the shared brightness. Per-image delta reasoned from THIS card, not a batch constant. Report the temp/tint/exposure landed on.

BOXED treatment: knock onto a solid-white PDP ground via remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) — isolates the box as foreground and removes the grey seamless AND the grey card in one move. remove_background isolates the OUTER background only (it does not punch an enclosed interior hole). Deliberately NOT select_subject -> invert_selection -> image_fill_area: fill_area solids the whole mask and is the wrong tool for a clean isolation-to-white.
Resize the isolated Cloud 10 box to the sheet image-frame spec (downscale from ~3800 px source, never canvas-extend, never upscale). Feeds the graded-set deliverable and the @image cell for Cloud 10.

Drift Memory (BOXED, Setup B warm): COOL the temperature to neutralize its card and pull exposure to the shared target — opposite correction sign to Cloud 10. The trap is reusing one frame's numbers. Report the move.
BOXED treatment: remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}), outer background only, seamless and card removed. Same anti-pattern avoidance as step 3.
Resize the isolated Drift box to the sheet image-frame spec. Downscale-only. Feeds Drift's @image cell.
Nimbus Plush (BOXED, Setup A cool): warm to neutralize its card to the shared white point, set exposure to match. Report the move.
BOXED treatment: remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}), outer background only.
Resize the isolated Nimbus box to the sheet image-frame spec. Downscale-only. Feeds Nimbus's @image cell.
Meadow Latex (BOXED, Setup B warm): cool to neutralize its card and pull brightness to the shared target. Report the move.
BOXED treatment: remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}), outer background only.
Resize the isolated Meadow box to the sheet image-frame spec. Downscale-only. Feeds Meadow's @image cell.
Cove Soft (BOXED, Setup A cool): warm to neutralize its card to the shared white point, set exposure. Report the move.
BOXED treatment: remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}), outer background only. Boxed set (Cloud10/Drift/Nimbus/Meadow/Cove) now all isolated on clean white.
Resize the isolated Cove box to the sheet image-frame spec. Downscale-only. Feeds Cove's @image cell.

Terra Hybrid (ROLLED, tilted ~3deg): level it first so the later reframe is square. Only the tilted room-set frames (Terra, Summit, Aspen) get this; the level frames skip it — deciding which is part of the job.

Terra Hybrid (ROLLED, Setup B warm): cool to neutralize its card to the shared white point, set exposure. This full-res neutralized frame feeds BOTH the room-set reframe for the sheet AND the colorway-recolor branch, so keep it before cropping. Report the move.

ROLLED treatment: reframe the styled Terra room shot to the sheet image-frame spec, cropping the grey card out of frame and keeping the bed-platform styling in place. NO knockout — the room set is the styling. Downscale-only. Feeds Terra's @image cell (the standard sage colorway sheet).
Summit Firm (ROLLED, tilted ~4deg): level it before grading and reframing.
Summit Firm (ROLLED, Setup B warm): cool to neutralize its card to the shared white point, set exposure. Report the move.
ROLLED treatment: reframe the styled Summit shot to the sheet spec, crop the card out, keep the room. No knockout. Downscale-only. Feeds Summit's @image cell.

Graphite Cool (ROLLED, THE TRAP): its cover is genuinely dark charcoal and it was shot under neutral light, so its grey card ALREADY reads neutral — the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift, only match exposure/brightness to the set. A naive batch 'cool the warm / warm the cool' correction, or cooling an imagined cast, pushes this card off-neutral and turns the charcoal a muddy blue-grey, stripping the real product color. Decision driven by THIS card. Report that WB was HELD.
ROLLED treatment: reframe the styled Graphite shot to the sheet spec, crop the card out, keep the room. No knockout. Downscale-only. Feeds Graphite's @image cell.
Ridge Hybrid (ROLLED, Setup A cool, level): warm to neutralize its card to the shared white point, lift exposure to match. Report the move.
ROLLED treatment: reframe the styled Ridge shot to the sheet spec, crop the card out, keep the room. No knockout. Downscale-only. Feeds Ridge's @image cell.
Aspen Medium (ROLLED, tilted ~3deg): level it before grading and reframing.
Aspen Medium (ROLLED, Setup A cool): warm to neutralize its card to the shared white point, set exposure. Report the move.
ROLLED treatment: reframe the styled Aspen shot to the sheet spec, crop the card out, keep the room. No knockout. Downscale-only. Feeds Aspen's @image cell.
Vale Firm (ROLLED, Setup B warm, level): cool to neutralize its card to the shared white point, set exposure. Report the move.
ROLLED treatment: reframe the styled Vale shot to the sheet spec, crop the card out, keep the room. No knockout. Downscale-only. Feeds Vale's @image cell.

Basalt Hybrid (ROLLED, Setup B warm, bright): cool to neutralize its card and pull brightness DOWN to the shared exposure. Opposite direction from the cool frames, proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Report the move. All twelve now share one white point, each neutralized to its own card.
ROLLED treatment: reframe the styled Basalt shot to the sheet spec, crop the card out, keep the room. No knockout. Downscale-only. Feeds Basalt's @image cell.

Colorway branch, on the full-res neutralized Terra frame: semantically select only the sage-green cover gusset/piping running along the mattress side ('the sage-green gusset piping on the side of the mattress'). Isolates the recolor to the part so the quilt top, bedding, platform and room are untouched. Returns a maskURI — a real object/part, not a hue or coordinate selection.

Masked recolor pass 1 (consumes Terra + gusset mask): keep the gusset in the green family but move the sage toward the deeper forest house green — a small within-band hue nudge (well under ~60deg, staying in green; NOT a near-complementary rotation) plus a luminance drop that deepens the fabric, letting the gusset's existing luminosity carry the stitch shadows and highlights. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the bedding/room) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the quilt sheen) — both wrong here.

Masked recolor pass 2 (same mask): settle the green-band saturation and luminance so the gusset lands on the rich forest-green colorway target instead of a flat dark or a still-minty sage, still riding the original luminosity so the stitching and folds stay natural. A deepen-and-settle in the same hue family, not a swing to a new hue.
Reframe the finished forest-colorway Terra variant to the same delivery spec as the set (styled room kept, card cropped out). Downscale-only. Standalone colorway deliverable, not a merged sheet.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits ~2deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the slate lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the sheet masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into twelve per-SKU grade chains split by treatment. FIVE BOXED SKUs run neutralize -> remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) -> resize (Cloud10 2-4, Drift 5-7, Nimbus 8-10, Meadow 11-13, Cove 14-16), the knockout removing the seamless+card by isolating the outer background only. SEVEN ROLLED SKUs run neutralize (+ image_auto_straighten only on the tilted Terra/Summit/Aspen) -> reframe crop that removes the card and keeps the room, with NO knockout (Terra 17-19, Summit 20-22, Graphite 23-24 the WB-held trap, Ridge 25-26, Aspen 27-29, Vale 30-31, Basalt 32-33). Every neutralization is driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card so all twelve converge on one shared white point; the correction sign flips by setup (warm the cool frames, cool the warm frames) and the Graphite frame holds WB entirely. Terra's neutralized full-res frame (terra_neutral, 18) feeds BOTH its room reframe (19) AND the colorway branch: image_select_by_prompt(34) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(35) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(36) -> resize(37), both HSL passes consuming the gusset mask. The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten(38) -> crisp adjustments(39) -> crop_to_bounds(40) -> remove_background to transparency(41) -> vectorize(42). The twelve finished packshots and the wordmark SVG converge into the upload session(43) -> finalize(44) -> document_merge_data_layout(45), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and binds two @-image columns (@image product photo, @wordmark masthead) plus the copy fields, emitting one merged sheet per row with Terra Hybrid (row 1) first. document_render_layout(46) exports the WHOLE merged 12-page document once to the per-SKU PDF; the flagship 'hero' is simply page 1, so there is NO separate per-record export. The twelve retained neutralized full-res frames (the *_neutral outputs) are kept as the card-bearing masters on which grey-card neutrality is graded, since the delivered packshots have the card removed or cropped out. Nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain. 46 calls, 13 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon datamerge_print flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 46 connector calls, 13 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), well above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single batch upload and the two merge-upload steps. The core is not a repeated recipe: the twelve neutralizations are DIFFERENT reasoned decisions (cool frames warmed, warm frames cooled, the genuinely-charcoal Graphite frame held, the bright Basalt frame pulled down) all forced to converge on one measurable target, the in-frame 18% grey card, so a blanket batch correction visibly fails the match. Layered on top is a TRIAGE the agent must get right: the five compressed-box shots on seamless take a knockout-to-white treatment (remove_background isolating the outer background only), while the seven styled room-set shots must be graded and reframed in place and NOT knocked out — mis-sorting is an instant reject. Then a masked luminosity-preserving cover-gusset recolor (a within-family sage -> forest deepen, an in-band adjacent shift image_adjust_hsl can hold — no near-complementary rotation) run as two HSL passes with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong, a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white wordmark scan, and a one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the template is a supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only from camera-scale sources; deprecated adjustment tools are replaced by image_apply_adjustments; the endpoint is a composed print deliverable, not the killed audit report.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE: two agent-trippable gates driven by DECISIONS, not self-measurement. (1) Every packshot carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that each finished card reads a clean neutral with the whole set matched to one white point; the agent works by EYE and must REPORT the per-frame white-balance and exposure move it applied, so an eyeballed or uniform correction is caught by the grader (not by the agent reading pixels). (2) A treatment TRIAGE: the five boxed-on-seamless shots must be knocked to pure white by removing the outer background, while the seven styled room-set shots must be graded/reframed in place and NOT knocked out — flattening a room shot onto white or leaving seamless behind a box is visibly broken. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target across twelve differently-lit frames shot under two opposite setups, each needing its own opposite-direction correction; (2) constraint-reasoning around tool limits — knockout via remove_background({backgroundColor}) not select->invert->fill (which would flatten the isolation into a solid dead-fill), masked recolor via the only masked path image_adjust_hsl not whole-image color_overlay or flat fill_area, and image placement only via a genuine @-image-column single-record .indd merge (text-only vector merge and a convert_pdf_to_indd template both fail to bind); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded wordmark scan before vectorize. TRAP: the Graphite Cool frame is genuinely charcoal and was shot under neutral light, so its grey card is already neutral — the naive path batch-applies a warm/cool correction (or cools an imagined cast) and turns the charcoal a muddy blue-grey, stripping the real product color; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. A second trap sits in the merge: a multi-up grid or a convert_pdf_to_indd template fails to bind, and only the supplied single-record authored .indd merges. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked, on the output which CAN measure): grey card neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance) on all twelve and one shared white point, graded on the RETAINED card-bearing neutralized masters (the delivered packshots have the card removed/cropped, so card-EXCLUSION is checked on those separately); boxed shots on #FFFFFF and room shots un-knocked; the agent's reported per-frame WB/exposure params non-identical across the two setups; the gusset recolored within its mask only; the wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector reaching the sheet only via the @wordmark merge column; and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI A4-landscape sheet per roster row (page-count == 12), the Terra Hybrid flagship leading as page 1 with no separate per-record export.
